articles.title: Chicago Makes A Statement: 3 Takeaways From The Bears' Win Over The Seahawks
articles.summary: The Bears made a statement with a win on the road against the reigning-champion Seahawks. Here are our takeaways.
articles.body: The Chicago Bears traveled to the Pacific Northwest looking for a signature victory to show they are a Super Bowl-caliber team. In the strength of a crisp offense led by head coach Ben Johnson and an impressive performance by their defense, the Bears earned a 34-17 victory in a slugfest over the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Monday night. The Bears (6-2) moved within one-half game of the first-place Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in the NFC North, while the Seahawks dropped into a second-place tie with the Los Angeles Rams (4-4). Both teams are well behind the NFC West-leading San Francisco 49ers (6-1). Here are my takeaways: 1.Caleb Williams Breaks Through Against Seattle Defense Williams and Chicago’s offense grabbed control of the game from the start, driving 80 yards on 17 plays that were capped by a 1-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden III. Williams finished 8-of-10 for 58 yards and a score on that scoring drive. After that first drive, the Bears went three-and-out on their next two possessions and had a punt partially blocked, which still traveled 45 yards, fortunately for Chicago. But the Bears cranked up the offense after that by leaning on Williams and the passing game. The former USC star finished 24-of-34 for 247 yards with a touchdown pass and no interceptions. Williams completed passes to seven different receivers and posted a 101.0 passer rating. Williams is the first QB to throw for more than 200 passing yards against the Seahawks this season. Bears tight end Colston Loveland led the Bears with seven receptions for 65 yards, while D’Andre Swift finished with 61 rushing yards on 25 carries and three scores. The 34 points are the most Seattle’s defense has given up this season. 2.Jeffery Simmons Adds Juice To Chicago's Defense The Bears gave up two first-round picks as part of the package to secure the services of one of the best defensive tackles in the NFL from the Tennessee Titans in Simmons. Through one game, Chicago must be pleased with the deal. Simmons led the Bears with six combined tackles – including two tackles for a loss – a sack and a pass breakup. Simmons played 49 (85.7%) of Chicago’s defensive snaps. He led a ferocious Chicago pass rush that had Sam Darnold running for cover most of the evening. The Bears sacked Darnold three times and created a 31 % pressure rate, according to Next Gen Stats. 3.Sam Darnold's Turnover Issues Persist The turnover bug plagued the USC product again, as Darnold had an attempted pass deflected by the Bears' Austin Booker at the line of scrimmage and intercepted by fellow defensive lineman James Lynch. The turnover was Darnold’s ninth interception this season. Only Justin Herbert (10) has more. Darnold has had an interception in every game he’s played this season. The Seahawks couldn’t get much going on offense, other than the team’s top playmaker in wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The Ohio State product finished with six catches for 118 yards, including a 43-yard touchdown pass on a double move at the end of the first half. However, Smith-Njigba was also called for offensive pass interference for the first time in his career, on a play that would have given the Seahawks first-and-goal from Chicago’s 1-yard line at the end of the third quarter. The Seahawks didn’t get anything on the drive after a Jason Myers field goal was blocked by the Bears. Seattle finished with just 252 total yards as a team and struggled to get touchdowns in the red zone. Seattle finished 0-for-3 in the red zone last week against the Kansas City Chiefs and 1-for-3 against the Bears. Seattle is under 50% for the season and ranks fifth worst in the league. Even the addition of running backs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet did not improve Seattle’s running game, as Chicago held the Seahawks to 81 rushing yards. 3 ½. What's Next? The Bears are back in primetime next week on Sunday night. They'll face a Buccaneers team that became the first team since 1974 to win a game without completing a pass. The Seahawks, having lost three of their last four games, take on the upstart Cardinals in what suddenly is a very important game. If Arizona wins next Sunday, it will be tied at 4-5 with Seattle.

articles.title: Josh Allen incident puts Ravens’ $100 million star at risk of NFL discipline as league reviews controversial moment
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith could face another NFL fine after his controversial contact with Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen sparked
articles.body: Baltimore Ravens linebacker Roquan Smith could face another NFL fine after his controversial contact with Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen sparked criticism following Sunday's 36-10 defeat. Smith appeared to grab Allen's facemask and pull his head backward during a fourth-quarter sneak, but officials allowed the touchdown to stand without throwing a flag. The incident has drawn attention beyond the result, particularly because Smith was fined for a similar play earlier this season. With his disciplinary record now under scrutiny, the three-time All-Pro could face a more expensive penalty.Roquan Smith faces fresh NFL scrutiny after Josh Allen incidentThe incident happened during Buffalo's opening possession. The Bills had reached the goal line and attempted a quarterback sneak with Allen on third down, but Baltimore's defense stopped him short. Buffalo tried again on fourth down, and Allen managed to cross the goal line for the touchdown.However, replays showed Smith grabbing the quarterback's facemask and pulling his head backward as the play unfolded. The officials did not penalize the Ravens linebacker, allowing the touchdown to stand.Allen showed no apparent signs of injury and continued playing. He eventually finished the game with two passing touchdowns and a rushing score as Buffalo secured a comfortable victory.The footage quickly became a talking point among Bills supporters. Dave Myers of the Built in Buffalo podcast was particularly critical of Smith's actions and questioned why the linebacker had not received a suspension.“There’s dirty players, then there is Roquan Smith,” Myers said. “Dude should be suspended for trying to pull Josh Allen’s head off.”That reaction has added pressure on the NFL to examine the play. However, there has been no confirmed announcement of a new fine or suspension against Smith.His previous fine against Tyler Shough makes the situation worseWhat makes the latest incident more concerning for Smith is its similarity to an earlier play involving New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough.During Baltimore's 24-17 defeat to New Orleans on September 20, Shough scored a late fourth-down rushing touchdown with 1:28 remaining. Smith was again accused of grabbing the quarterback's facemask during the goal-line attempt.Officials missed the penalty during the game, but the NFL reviewed the footage and fined Smith $11,941. The decision established a disciplinary precedent that could now work against the Ravens linebacker.According to Heavy, another facemask violation this season could push his fine to $17,911. Smith has also received previous fines for roughing the passer, a horse-collar tackle and another facemask incident.He has never been suspended or ejected during his NFL career. That distinction could become important if the league considers whether his recent actions point to a repeated problem rather than an isolated mistake.Ravens fans defend Smith despite growing criticismThe reaction has not been entirely against the Baltimore linebacker. Some Ravens supporters believe Buffalo's decision to repeatedly use Allen on quarterback sneaks exposes its star quarterback to unnecessary physical contact.One fan wrote, “You are running a rugby play and crying that your QB is getting hit in a contact sport! Grow up.”Another added, “Josh Allen does silly stuff and is protected by the rules. He gets hurt; it’s on him.”The disagreement highlights an important distinction. Quarterback sneaks are legal, but defenders must still follow the league's rules on unnecessary contact and player safety. The physical nature of the play does not automatically excuse a facemask grab.Smith signed a five-year, $100 million extension with Baltimore in 2023, becoming the highest-paid off-ball linebacker in NFL history at the time. His contract reflects his importance to the defense, but his value to the Ravens also makes any potential suspension a bigger concern.Baltimore already has problems after losing three consecutive games and falling to 4-4. With Lamar Jackson facing surgery on his right thumb, another setback involving Smith would create an additional headache for the team. The linebacker now faces a difficult week, with his previous punishment making the latest incident harder to dismiss.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Explains Cowboys' Approach on Coaching Salaries, 'Zero Correlation' to Winning
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones pushed back against the narrative that paying a head coach more money would immediately translate to success on the field.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones pushed back against the narrative that paying a head coach more money would immediately translate to success on the field.

"There's zero correlation between how much you pay a coach or how many coaches you have, as to winning. There's no correlation," he said Tuesday in an appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

Coaches are no different from players in that some who are highly paid won't deliver, while others far exceed their contracts. At the same time, it's often true that a coach's earnings, as with athletes, reflect what they have achieved already.

Andy Reid, John Harbaugh and Sean Payton are all the joint highest-paid coaches in the NFL at $20 million annually, according to Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen . Sean McVay and Kyle Shanahan are next on the list at $19 million.

Each of those five coaches has been a consistent winner, and Shanahan is the only one without a Super Bowl title.

Contrast that with the fact that Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer didn't even make the top 15 on Badenhausen's list. That's not a big surprise when he had been a career coordinator before Dallas promoted him.

Jones' critics and disgruntled fans will say his remarks illustrate a wider flaw in his approach.

There are countless examples in a given season of how much a good coach can elevate a franchise. It matters.

Hiring Bill Parcells in 2003 is arguably the last time Dallas took a big swing on a coach. Mike McCarthy was a former Super Bowl champion, but his stock had fallen toward the end of his tenure with the Green Bay Packers.

Jones appears averse to paying what it takes or ceding enough authority to a young coordinator on the rise or top-tier head coach who's out of work. Imagine what might've happened if the Cowboys landed Ben Johnson or Mike Vrabel during the 2025 hiring cycle.

Instead, Dallas settled on Schottenheimer, and the results have been predictably underwhelming.

Don't expect Jones' mindset to change if Schottenheimer gets the boot at some point.

articles.title: A $6M house for a $995k problem: How one viral relationship forced Travis Kelce to rethink where he sleeps
articles.summary: Travis Kelce paid $995,000 for a custom home in Kansas City in 2019. Four years later, he closed on a $6 million gated estate in Leawood, Kansas.
articles.body: Travis Kelce paid $995,000 for a custom home in Kansas City in 2019. Four years later, he closed on a $6 million gated estate in Leawood, Kansas. The turning point came on September 24, 2023, when Taylor Swift attended her first Chiefs game. Three days later, Kelce told his brother on their podcast that photographers had started showing up outside his house. TMZ reported the purchase less than four weeks after that game. The speed makes it look like a snap decision. The record shows something more layered.Why did Travis Kelce trade a $995k home for a $6M mansion?Because Taylor Swift’s arrival turned an old inconvenience into a daily problem. Kelce bought his Briarcliff West home in 2019. Fox Business described it as a custom, seven-bedroom house of about 4,200 square feet, reachable by street. That suited a Chiefs star with a loyal local following. It suited him less once photographers started tracking his dating life.The timeline moves quickly. Swift attended her first Chiefs game on September 24, 2023. Three days later, on the September 27 episode of New Heights, Kelce told his brother Jason, “Like paparazzi outside my house. They all have British accents, too.” He was joking, but the problem was real. The couple’s first public outing came October 15 in New York, and TMZ reported the purchase a few days after that.Still, this was not purely a Swift story. Local reporting at the time noted that rumors of Kelce leaving Briarcliff had circulated for months, long before she appeared. The Leawood house had also been listed since September 2022, so it was already waiting. Cash deals can close quickly, and Inman reported that Kelce paid cash, so the speed of the sale does not prove much on its own. The likelier reading is that Swift sped up a decision more than she created one.What was wrong with Kelce’s old Kansas City house?Access, mostly. The Briarcliff home was easy to reach from the street, and that made it simple for anyone to park nearby and watch. TMZ’s sources said the house was turning into a “tourist attraction,” Newsweek reported. Fans came by. Photographers came by. A Daily Mail video, apparently shot by a neighbor, showed Swift leaving his home before a game at Arrowhead.Neighbors felt it too. They reportedly were not happy about the added attention. On Halloween night, photos obtained by the Daily Mail showed Kelce’s home blocked off with caution tape, apparently to keep trick-or-treaters away, and a security guard sat in a car outside the driveway. An upscale residential street had become a destination.An insider told the New York Post that Kelce also felt self-conscious about how modest the house looked once he started dating Swift. Treat that as gossip, since it came from an unnamed source. Still, it hints at a second pressure beyond security: image.Did the gated Leawood estate actually solve the problem?Partly. On paper, the new address fixed the access problem. The estate sits in the gated Tomahawk Creek Estates community at the end of a cul-de-sac, on more than three acres, about 15 miles from Arrowhead, Fox Business reported. Some Chiefs fans had hoped he would follow Patrick Mahomes to Loch Lloyd, another gated community. He chose Johnson County instead.The amenities fit the same logic. The listing promised a lighted tennis and pickleball court, a mini-golf course with a practice green, a pool with a waterfall, a wine cellar and a six-car garage. In September, according to Entrepreneur, the couple reportedly paid every diner’s check at a downtown Kansas City restaurant to get some privacy. When a night out means buying out the room, a house that brings the night in starts to look practical.Reality was messier. Jason Kelce said on The Big Podcast with Shaq in early 2024 that Travis had to leave his old house because fans kept hanging around it. The new house got tested right away. On the first day in the gated community, Jason said, “somebody knocks on the back window of the house.” So the gate bought distance from the street, not from curiosity.It did not stop everything else, either. A Leawood police report showed someone broke into the home just after 7:30 p.m. on October 7, 2024, the night the Chiefs played the Saints on Monday Night Football, and took $20,000 in cash. A back door was damaged, and the report listed total losses and damage at $21,000.What does the price gap say about the cost of fame?Start with the math. Kelce paid $995,000 for the Briarcliff home in 2019 and $5,999,950 for the Leawood estate in 2023, about six times as much. Deal records put the new house at 16,921 square feet, roughly four times the old one if the 4,200 figure is right. That works out to about $237 per square foot in 2019 and $355 in 2023.Four years of rising prices and the extra acreage explain part of that gap. The rest probably pays for things no listing can quantify: a gate, a dead-end street and fewer strangers at the door. For a player whose home life suddenly drew crowds, that is a fair trade. It is also an expensive one.The house hunt did not end there. In March 2026, Kelce closed on a $5.35 million lakefront mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio, near his hometown of Cleveland Heights, the Wall Street Journal reported. News 5 Cleveland noted that rumors of a second home in Northeast Ohio had flown for more than a year. He married Swift in July, and the couple now hold property in Kansas, Tennessee, Rhode Island, New York, California and Ohio, ESPN reported.The Briarcliff West house is still part of the picture. One early-2026 report said property records indicate Kelce still owns it. The house he bought for $995,000 still stands where it always did. What changed was how many people were looking at it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “I’m someone who does care”: Travis Kelce opens up about about the pressure of constant public judgment as he tries to stay focused on his career
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, has been one of the most popular players in the league for the last decade but he has experienced global
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, has been one of the most popular players in the league for the last decade but he has experienced global fame in the last few years. While he has remained focused on his career, there has also been a lot of negativity related to his name. Amid the new season, the Super Bowl champion Travis Kelce opens up about how it has affected him.Travis Kelce reflects on how the negativity surrounding his life has continued to affect him even as he remains privateIn an interview with GQ Magazine, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, Travis Kelce opened up about how he deals with hate as he said, “You can’t block that out…”The 37 year old star player added, “If someone says something that they don’t like about you, you have to be able to understand how you are portraying yourself for them to say that. I’m a guy who doesn’t want anyone to say anything negative about me. Some people don’t give a fuck. I’m someone who does care.”Travis Kelce continued, “I do want people to look at me like I’m doing good in the world, I’m influencing and using my platform for the better, being a role model, being somebody that has done it the right way.”The popular tight end added, “I joke about it. It is what it is. I’m just out here living life,” he says. “I don’t necessarily want everyone to think that I’m an idiot…There’s always something to learn. Acting like you’re the smartest one in the room just isn’t the way to go.”While Travis Kelce has tried to keep his personal life out of the spotlight, he has constantly dealt with negative rumors about himself and his family.It has been roughly four months since Travis Kelce tied the knot and he has continued to remain strictly private about it. No pictures or videos from their high profile wedding have been leaked to the media.Travis Kelce keeps his mind on the field and his performance even as he remains surrounded by constant judgementDespite the constant judgement he faces, the popular tight end Travis Kelce has continued to remain focused on his career on the field even though he dealt with many rumors about a potential retirement.After a pretty slow run on the field in the last few years, the 37 year old tight end has bounced back well as Travis Kelce has broken records this time.With the Kansas City Chiefs recording two losses consecutively this time, all eyes remain on Travis Kelce as he has been emotional about the team’s performance and has assured that they will bounce back.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Lamar Jackson's latest injury sparks Colin Cowherd's blunt Ravens warning over quarterback's future and contract extension
articles.summary: Colin Cowherd has questioned whether the Baltimore Ravens should offer Lamar Jackson another contract extension after the quarterback suffered a serious
articles.body: Colin Cowherd has questioned whether the Baltimore Ravens should offer Lamar Jackson another contract extension after the quarterback suffered a serious thumb injury. Jackson needs surgery and will miss at least four games, with head coach Jesse Minter admitting that his season could be over. Cowherd believes Jackson’s repeated injury problems and missed games have made a long-term commitment difficult for Baltimore.Colin Cowherd says Lamar Jackson’s injury record makes another Ravens contract extension difficultCowherd made his position clear during an episode of The Herd, arguing that Baltimore should think carefully before giving Jackson another big contract. He said a quarterback’s salary should reflect how much he produces and how often he is available to play. In his view, Jackson’s recent injury problems have changed the way the Ravens must look at his future.“For any great player in this league, especially quarterbacks, there is a sliding scale, and the scale is: What can I pay you based on what you’re producing? You can’t extend Lamar Jackson. I’m not blaming him for being able to play one play before he got hurt. I’m not blaming him. That’s his reality.”Cowherd also pointed to the number of times Jackson has used his legs to make plays, suggesting that his playing style has added to the physical demands of his position.“Between the moods and the injuries, he has 200 more rushes than any quarterback in the league since he entered it. And annually now, is he practicing? Is he playing? The team doesn’t know. I’m not blaming him for the injury, but injuries are now part of the story.”The commentator then explained why he believes Baltimore should be careful about making another major financial commitment to its quarterback.“Listen, here’s Lamar’s current reality: I’m not pointing fingers, but less available, less productive. I’m going to struggle tying my franchise to that.”Jackson signed a five-year, $260 million contract extension with Baltimore in 2023. His next contract decision is becoming a bigger subject of discussion as his current deal continues, especially with his availability now a concern. ESPN also reported in September that Jackson had been reluctant to discuss another long-term agreement with the Ravens.Lamar Jackson’s injury history adds to Baltimore Ravens’ contract concernsCowherd’s criticism was not limited to the latest thumb injury. He also questioned whether Jackson has been able to maintain the same level of play and availability over the last two seasons. The quarterback has missed several games because of injuries, making it harder for Baltimore to rely on him throughout a full season.“All I know is this. His speed last year, when clocked, was not the same. It feels like he’s getting hurt more often. I’m not blaming him. But for the first seven seasons, I always supported Lamar Jackson. I always said, ‘Guys, he won 75% of his starts.’ The last two years, nine and nine. A .500 quarterback. And again, at quarterback, it’s one thing if you’re a number three corner or a number two tight end. The entire franchise is built around you.”He also brought up Josh Allen and Justin Herbert while discussing the physical demands on NFL quarterbacks.“I’m not saying guys don’t get injured. Maybe you just say it’s wacky, it’s coincidental. Well, here’s what I know: Josh Allen never gets hurt. Here’s what I know: Justin Herbert’s taking a beating, and he’s up. Not playing well, but he’s up.”Jackson’s injury history gives some context to Cowherd’s concerns. In 2021, a right ankle injury kept him out of Baltimore’s final four regular-season games. The following year, a PCL sprain in his knee forced him to miss the final five regular-season games and the Ravens’ playoff loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.He managed to play the full 2024 regular season, but the 2025 campaign brought more problems. A hamstring injury cost him three games, while a back injury kept him out of another. This season, he had already missed three games with an ankle injury before hurting his right thumb against Buffalo.According to the Baltimore Ravens’ November 2 injury update, Jackson had not undergone surgery yet and was headed for injured reserve. The team also had concerns about backup Tyler Huntley’s toe injury, leaving rookie Joe Fagnano as another option at quarterback.Baltimore is now 4-4 and faces the Jacksonville Jaguars on November 5. With Jackson expected to miss at least four games, the Ravens must prepare for an important stretch without their two-time MVP.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' road to another Super Bowl grows tougher as Kansas City Chiefs struggle to regain their championship form
articles.summary: Kansas City started 5-0 and has now lost twice in a row.
articles.body: Kansas City started 5-0 and has now lost twice in a row. A 20-3 defeat at Seattle was followed by a 28-24 loss at Denver, a game the Chiefs led by double digits in the fourth quarter. At 5-2, they have slipped to second in the AFC West for the first time this season. Patrick Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Denver, and it still was not enough. The New York Jets visit Arrowhead on Sunday, and the Chiefs badly need a clean win to settle things.Why have the Chiefs not regained their championship form?On paper, 5-2 is a fine record. Underneath, the numbers tell a different story. Kansas City led the NFL in total yards per game at 414 before Seattle held it to 213. Mahomes finished with 165 passing yards and an interception behind an injury-hit offensive line. Kenneth Walker III, the free agent signed to drive the run game, managed 36 yards. Andy Reid did not dodge it. “I take full responsibility for this,” he said. Mahomes was equally frustrated and made no effort to hide it.Denver exposed a different flaw. The offense moved the ball, and Mahomes passed Peyton Manning and Dan Marino with his 49th game of three or more touchdown passes, the most by any player in his first 10 seasons. Then the lead slipped away. Mahomes had lost only twice before when ahead by double digits in the fourth quarter. Now it is three times, against 80 wins. One loss does not define a career, but it hints at a team still working out how to close games without its old margin for error.What does the road back to the Super Bowl look like now?Context makes the climb steeper. Kansas City went 6-11 last year and missed the playoffs after Mahomes tore his ACL in Week 15. He came back this fall with an extension through 2033, and Travis Kelce re-signed on a new three-year deal. The 5-0 start made that comeback look smooth. These two losses have reopened questions about the offensive line and the depth around the quarterback. Two games do not make a collapse, but the margin for error is shrinking.The schedule offers a quick chance to answer them. The Jets visit Arrowhead on Sunday. Buffalo awaits in Week 12, and a meeting with Josh Allen will say plenty about where this team really stands. Before then, Kansas City has to protect Mahomes and bring back the ground game that carried it early. Walker ran for 173 yards in Week 1 and 177 in Week 4. He has not come close to those numbers in the last two games.Reid has to decide how much he leans on quicker throws and designed runs while the line is thin. Seattle showed how costly long dropbacks can be. Sunday gives him a chance to try it before the schedule gets harder.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback, has remained a committed player on the field while being a dedicated father to his three children and a loving husband to his wife, Brittany Mahomes. Patrick Mahomes has enjoyed a successful career but his family life is just as important for him as he has opened up about it.Patrick Mahomes opens up about being a father as he manages his busy career on the fieldIn an interview, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player Patrick Mahomes said, “Everybody sees the game days. They don’t see the day-to-day grind. They don’t see how you have to manage playing football and being a dad and being a husband.”The star player explained how he has prioritized his family as he added, “It’s football. You’re gonna have highs; you’re gonna have the lows…You put so much into this that you want to win, you want to succeed. And you want to win that Super Bowl at the end of the year…”The popular quarterback continued, “But I have to be a dad too. I have to be a husband.”Ever since Patrick Mahomes was drafted by the Kansas City Chiefs, he has been public about how his family comes first for him.Through all the challenging days in his professional life, Patrick Mahomes has always sought support from his wife, Brittany Mahomes, and their three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden Raye.Patrick Mahomes’ wife Britany Mahomes has also been there for him since the beginning and has even defended him against critics.Over the last few years, Patrick Mahomes and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, love and commitment to each other have inspired billions around the world.Patrick Mahomes reflects on the team’s performance as the Kansas City Chiefs struggl on the fieldFor now, all eyes remain on Patrick Mahomes as he navigates through a tough time after the Kansas City Chiefs recorded two consecutive losses against the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos.A few hours ago, as the top quarterback spoke to reporters, he said, "Now, you're kind of in a dogfight for the division… You have to take it one week at a time…”The popular star added, “Last week we didn't have the fight that we had this week. I thought the fight was better this week. Whenever you're playing up against a really good football team. But at the end a loss is a loss and you learn from it, you move on from it and we're still early in the season."Patrick Mahomes seems busy preparing for the upcoming clash as all eyes remain on him amid concerns that the team is clearly struggling on the field in the new season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: FSU students react to Mike Norvell's firing as nearly $50 million buyout triggers unexpected debate over Florida State's decision
articles.summary: Florida State students have shared mixed reactions after the university fired head coach Mike Norvell despite facing a buyout of nearly $50 million.
articles.body: Florida State students have shared mixed reactions after the university fired head coach Mike Norvell despite facing a buyout of nearly $50 million. While some believe the decision was necessary to help the Seminoles recover, others have questioned why the university waited until the middle of the season. Students also have different views on whether making the coaching change now will help the team prepare for next year.FSU students support Mike Norvell’s firing despite massive buyoutAccording to WCTV reporter Julia Miller, students and alumni had different opinions about Norvell’s departure when she spoke to them in Tallahassee. Some supported the university’s decision, believing that keeping him would only delay the team’s progress.One junior at Florida State said he was happy with the decision and felt the university might as well make the change now if it had already decided to pay Norvell his buyout.“I’m really happy about it. I mean, you were going to have to pay him the money regardless; might as well get him out of here now while we still have time to hopefully find a better head coach.”FSU alumna Grace Froehle also supported the move. She believes the coaching change could improve the team’s mood and give the university more time to find its next head coach before the 2027 season.“I think it’s better overall. I think it’s honestly good for the team. I think the morale of the team will be better, and the earlier we can get him fired, the sooner we can start recruiting for next year.”However, not every student agreed with that view. Junior Kyle Dastur questioned why Florida State chose to fire Norvell during the season instead of making the decision earlier.“It’s kind of stupid, like I don’t see the reason for firing him mid-season if we didn’t fire him at the start. I don’t get what that’s going to do.”The different reactions show that while some students are ready for a fresh start, others are unsure whether changing coaches with several games still left was the right move.Mike Norvell’s Florida state record and $50.3 million buyout explainedNorvell joined Florida State in December 2019 after spending four seasons as the head coach at Memphis. His first few years showed signs of progress, with the Seminoles improving from a 5-7 record in 2021 to 10-3 in 2022. The biggest success of his time in Tallahassee came in 2023, when Florida State won the ACC Championship and finished the regular season unbeaten at 13-0. However, the team was left out of the College Football Playoff and later lost the Orange Bowl to Georgia.The results changed sharply after that season. Florida State finished 2-10 in 2024 and then went 5-7 in 2025, missing bowl eligibility for a second straight year. The 2026 season did not bring the improvement the university wanted, as the Seminoles fell to 3-5 after losing 36-24 to Clemson on October 31.Florida State announced Norvell’s firing on November 1, ending his seven-season run with a 41-39 overall record. His conference record stood at 23-30.The financial side of the decision is also important. Before the 2024 season, Norvell signed an eight-year contract extension worth more than $84 million, keeping him at Florida State through 2031. The agreement included a clause requiring the university to pay 85% of his remaining salary if it fired him.Reports have placed the buyout at different figures. FOX Sports and the Associated Press put Norvell’s own buyout at around $47 million, while other reports have discussed a figure of more than $50 million when additional staff costs are included. On3 reported that the amount would have fallen to around $45.6 million if Florida State had waited until after the 2026 season.Despite the cost, the university decided not to wait. The move also means Florida State must begin looking for a permanent replacement, with assistant coach Rick Stockstill taking over as interim head coach.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update, Latest Rumors and Timeline to Return for Cardinals RB
articles.summary: Jeremiyah Love's difficult rookie season has only gotten worse.
articles.body:
Jeremiyah Love's difficult rookie season has only gotten worse.

The running back will go on injured reserve due to a high-ankle sprain, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network:

The issue is expected to hold him out four-to-five weeks.

Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur revealed on Monday that Love suffered a new ankle injury during the 33-30 overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys.

"It just stinks for him," LaFleur told reporters. "He wants to be out there helping his teammates. This guy loves ball. He just wants to contribute. He's such a team guy, such a coachable guy, he's such a likable guy. He just wants to be out there helping his guys. For him, going through what he's going through, it's adversity for sure, but he's gonna be stronger because of this."

Love, 21, has already dealt with ankle issues in both the preseason and during the regular season, with this latest issue affecting a different part of the ankle than his previous ailments.

Those injuries have hampered what was a much-anticipated rookie season from the No. 3 overall pick at the 2026 NFL draft. In six games Love has rushed for just 268 yards and a touchdown while adding 11 catches for 36 yards and another score.

Many fans—and fantasy football enthusiasts—expected Love to hit the ground running as Arizona's featured back, but that hasn't materialized. Instead he's operated in more of a platoon with Tyler Allgeier, and Sunday was his first game back after a two-game absence due to his ongoing ankle issues.

"I am myself when I got my ankles," Love told reporters last week. "I feel like, as a running back or as a receiver, a lot of the moves that we do with our ankles and knees and stuff like that, I like to come to complete stops. It impacted me quite a bit. ... I just want to go out there and be myself. I feel like the past few games, for really the whole season, I haven't really been able to go out there and just feel like myself. I just feel like I just can't go or I couldn't go out there and just do what I wanted to."

This latest ankle injury is yet another setback in that regard.

articles.title: Raiders' Mark Davis Talks 'Pressure' To Play Fernando Mendoza Over Kirk Cousins, Praises No. 1 Pick
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis said he's feeling "absolutely no pressure whatsoever" to start top overall pick Fernando Mendoza at quarterback this season during an interview on CNBC.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis said he's feeling "absolutely no pressure whatsoever" to start top overall pick Fernando Mendoza at quarterback this season during an interview on CNBC.

"Today, there's a lot of pressure put on teams when they draft a guy No. 1 that you have to play him right away," Davis continued (h/t Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal ). "That's why I think we were so fortunate to get Kirk Cousins as someone who could bridge the gap and let this young man learn a lot about what football is in the pros, the speed of the game and the things that have to be done. And he's picking it up great, but I think we're fortunate he doesn't have to go out and play."

Cousins, 38, has played well this season, throwing for 2,124 yards, 19 touchdowns and five interceptions while completing 63.6 percent of his passes and taking 11 sacks. The Raiders are 4-4 and right now are in the mix for a potential playoff berth, though five teams are currently ahead of them in the Wild Card hunt.

Nonetheless, it's given the Raiders little reason to rush Mendoza into action. And if they were going to make the change, doing so after their recent four-game losing streak would have been the time. But Cousins wasn't the main culprit during those struggles and just threw for 247 yards and three scores during a 38-33 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.

In other words, he's going to remain the guy for the time being.

articles.title: Pat McAfee makes bold Super Bowl prediction about $8.05 billion Jacksonville Jaguars after their dominant 5-2 start
articles.summary: Pat McAfee believes the Jacksonville Jaguars could become the surprise winners of Super Bowl LXI after their impressive start to the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body: Pat McAfee believes the Jacksonville Jaguars could become the surprise winners of Super Bowl LXI after their impressive start to the 2026 NFL season. Jacksonville improved to 5-2 following a convincing 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts on November 1. The team’s strong performances have also caught McAfee’s attention, as the ESPN host believes the Jaguars deserve more attention as serious title contenders.Pat McAfee backs Jacksonville Jaguars for Super Bowl LXI after 5-2 startThe Jacksonville Jaguars have given fans plenty of reasons to take them seriously this season, and Pat McAfee is among those who believe the team could go further than many expect. Speaking on his ESPN show, the former NFL punter made a bold prediction about Jacksonville’s chances of winning the Super Bowl.“Jacksonville Jaguars might win the Super Bowl and I don’t think anyone is saying that,” McAfee said.His comment came after the Jaguars produced another dominant performance at home, beating the Indianapolis Colts 42-7. The result moved Jacksonville to 5-2 and gave the team the best point differential in the NFL at plus-85. It also put them three games ahead of the Houston Texans in the AFC South standings.The Jaguars have been particularly difficult to stop at EverBank Stadium. Their victory over Indianapolis extended their regular-season home winning streak to seven games, with every win coming by at least 17 points. During this run, Jacksonville has outscored its opponents 271-75, showing how well its offense and defense have worked together.There was another impressive detail in Sunday’s performance. Jacksonville began the game with a 98-yard drive that lasted 12 plays and ended with a 12-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence to Brian Thomas Jr. It became the longest opening drive in franchise history.The win also extended Jacksonville’s home winning streak against Indianapolis to 12 games, making the Colts one of the teams that have struggled most against them at EverBank Stadium. Under head coach Liam Coen, the Jaguars have now scored at least 34 points in seven consecutive home victories. That run has tied an NFL record, previously achieved by the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Chargers.The franchise is also attracting attention off the field. According to Forbes’ September 2026 NFL team valuations, Jacksonville is worth an estimated $8.05 billion, making it the league’s 29th most valuable team. However, the biggest talking point right now is what the players are doing on the field.Trevor Lawrence and Bhayshul Tuten lead Jacksonville Jaguars’ Super Bowl hopesQuarterback Trevor Lawrence has played an important role in Jacksonville’s strong start. Against Indianapolis, he completed 10 of 14 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. His 153.3 passer rating was the highest of his career, and he finished the game with another performance that showed how dangerous he can be when the offense is working well.Through seven games, Lawrence has recorded 1,690 passing yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. His touchdown total puts him third among NFL quarterbacks, behind Joe Burrow with 20 and Kirk Cousins with 19. He has also recorded two games with a passer rating above 150 this season, making him the only quarterback in the league to achieve that mark twice.However, Lawrence has not been carrying the entire offense on his own. Running back Bhayshul Tuten also delivered a standout performance against the Colts, finishing with 104 rushing yards and one touchdown on 16 carries. He added 55 receiving yards and another touchdown on two catches.His performance made him the first player in Jaguars history to record at least 100 rushing yards, 50 receiving yards and a touchdown in both categories during the same game. Having Tuten contribute in both areas gives Jacksonville another way to trouble opposing defenses.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tom Brady Previews 'Emotional' Return to Patriots' Gillette Stadium for 1st Time as Broadcaster
articles.summary: Tom Brady is a New England Patriots legend, and he expects his return to Gillette Stadium as a broadcaster for the first time to be an "emotional" one.
articles.body:
Tom Brady is a New England Patriots legend, and he expects his return to Gillette Stadium as a broadcaster for the first time to be an "emotional" one.

"It'll be certainly emotional," Brady said during a conversation with Fox Sports' Colin Cowherd. "I mean every inch of that stadium I've been through so many times, from the locker rooms to the meeting rooms to the field. There are just so many memorable plays in that stadium, big games, championship games and rivalry games. Division-clinching games.

"To be back there and to really understand what that Patriot organization is all about and to convey that to the fans in a way where I'm not talking about myself, I'm really talking about this awesome program that's been built. The Patriots just always seem to do things the right way."

Brady will be the color commentator for Fox Sports' broadcast of Sunday's game between the Patriots and the Green Bay Packers.

What's more, Sunday will mark Rob Gronkowski's induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame. It is fitting that Brady will be in attendance seeing how they won four Super Bowls together, three of which came in New England.

The Patriots were the gold standard of the league for much of Brady's iconic tenure, winning six Super Bowls and reaching the game another three times. Brady went on to win another Lombardi Trophy with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and his seven Super Bowl titles are more than any single NFL franchise can claim.

While Brady finished his career with Tampa Bay, he is most closely associated with the Patriots.

And the team further cemented his legacy in 2025 when it unveiled his statue outside Gillette Stadium.

He will be back in person Sunday, and the fans will surely greet him with the warmest of welcomes after he brought the franchise so much sustained success.

articles.title: Ravens Sign New QB to Contract, Announce Week 9 Starter After Lamar Jackson & Tyler Huntley Injuries
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens signed quarterback Kedon Slovis to their roster, the team announced on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens signed quarterback Kedon Slovis to their roster, the team announced on Tuesday.

The 25-year-old quarterback was previously signed to the Green Bay Packers' practice squad.

In addition to signing Slovis, the Ravens announced rookie Joe Fagnano will start Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars:

Slovis began his professional career with the Indianapolis Colts as an undrafted free agent following the 2024 NFL Draft. In the following years, the BYU product bounced around the league for brief practice squad stints with the Houston Texans and Arizona Cardinals before landing with the Packers this offseason.

Slovis remains mostly an unknown on the field. He's only taken five snaps in the regular season, all of which came with the Arizona Cardinals during the 2025 season. Still, he provides Baltimore with much-needed relief at quarterback after a nightmarish game on Sunday left them with three injured quarterbacks.

Two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury on Baltimore's first offensive snap against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. The Ravens were forced to rely on the emergency third-stringer Fagnano after backup quarterback Tyler Huntley also went down with a toe injury during the 36-10 loss.

The Ravens had high hopes for the 2026 season, but their playoff aspirations have taken a significant blow. After a promising start to the season, Baltimore has lost three consecutive games to fall to a 4-4 record and last place in the AFC North.

articles.title: Peter King's new book 'The Game' sparks debate over NFL's most significant figures across four decades
articles.summary: Peter King's new book "The Game" ranks Bill Belichick at No. 24 and Don Shula outside the top 25 on his NFL Mount Rushmore of significance..
articles.body: The list of premier NFL historians has for a long time included Peter King as a contributor, and his new book titled "The Game" is a journey that gives color to the growth of America's sport from the 1980s, when baseball and the NFL were still sports landscape peers to the current day in which football simply dominates. King, the former Sports Illustrated writer and founding author of the Monday Morning Quarterback column, has delivered 40 chapters about King Sport. "The Game" is a journey that details everything from the perfect NFL career authored by a Steelers' player not part of the early-day Super Bowl titles, to the rebirth of the New York Giants in the 1980s, to the painful last stand of Bill Walsh, to the sad end of Al Davis in 2007 – with much in between and beyond. The book is a sprawling, colorful ride through four decades in forty chapters. FOOTBALL LEGEND BILL BELICHICK ADDRESSES HALL OF FAME SNUB AND WHETHER IT WAS A 'POLITICAL' DECISION Sitting down with the writer allowed me an opportunity to explain to King how wrong he was about his Mount Rushmore of Pro Football. Fine, so I didn't actually tell a legendary scribe he's wrong about his stuff. But it's fair to say I probed him about the water cooler conversation segment of the book, which he patterned after Mount Rushmore. Having known King for decades, I reminded him that Mount Rushmore has four presidents on its granite cliff and his Mount Rushmore boasts 100 people, then adds another 10 just because, then includes an honorable mention section. "Armando," King retorts, without missing a beat, "as you know, I always wrote long." Fair enough. Time to prod. King did not include either Bill Belichick or Don Shula among his top 20 names on his Mount Rushmore. EX-PATRIOTS STAR ON WHETHER TOM BRADY COULD FACE SAME HOF FATE AS BILL BELICHICK: 'CRAZY TO THINK ABOUT' Belichick, who has more Super Bowl championships than any other coach in NFL history, is No. 24 on King's mountain. "Well, my Mount Rushmore is about the people who have been most significant in making the NFL the monstrous game and product that it is today," King explains. "So, like I have Joe Carr, former NFL commissioner, as the 4th most significant guy in pro football history. NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL WILL NOT TESTIFY BEFORE CONGRESS AMID SCRUTINY OF PAST TESTIMONIES "I think it's hard for somebody, unless you're absolutely like the best who's ever done it, for me to say that he's more important in football history than, say, Lamar Hunt, or Pete Rozelle, or John Madden or Vince Lombardi ... And those are guys I have, obviously, in the top 10. "There are so many people, and I went through so many iterations of this, but I just tried to stick with the sort of the tried and true approach of people who were most responsible for this game being as gargantuan as it is." Before this gets out of control, understand that King was a Pro Football Hall of Fame selector for decades and thought it was a mistake not to induct Belichick as a first-ballot candidate. So he is not anti-Belichick, folks. MANNY FERNANDEZ, CORNERSTONE OF DOLPHINS’ PERFECT 1972 SEASON, DEAD AT 79 Shula, the winningest coach of all time and the architect of the NFL's only undefeated Super Bowl champion, is outside King's top 25. "I just don't think of Don Shula as a more important figure than the people I put above him," King said. "I think the reason is, and look, the undefeated season is obviously, that team is without peer in modern NFL history without any question. And that was an incredible accomplishment, especially because they beat some incredible teams in that season. They had a great year. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! "But I think the way I kind of look at it, other than the number of wins, which is paramount, when I look at Don Shula, I am left asking the question, 'What other contributions to the game did he have that should put him higher on this list? What are they?' "And I am left not convinced that he made the kind of contributions that guys like Madden and Lombardi made. This is more than just your win total. It has to do with everything you contributed to the game." King is a good sport allowing me to thrust and riposte with him a bit. Any book that can set off such an exchange over football is worth the time. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Daniel Jones Trade Landing Spots Floated by Adam Schefter amid Colts' Fire Sale at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, all while speculation continues around Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have already traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, all while speculation continues around Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs.

However, they could make a "curveball" trade ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 deadline.

ESPN's Adam Schefter suggested on the Adam Schefter Podcast that quarterback Daniel Jones could be a surprise trade candidate. He went as far as to list the Baltimore Ravens and Minnesota Vikings as potential landing spots.

"I know we're focused on Taylor and Downs, as we should be, and I'm not telling you that they're trading Daniel," Schefter said (10:40 mark). "I'm just telling you sometimes it's the curveball that you don't see."

Jones has just one season remaining on his deal past the 2026 campaign and has looked like anything but the Colts' long-term franchise quarterback this season. He has just five touchdown passes to nine interceptions, and the Colts are 2-6 in his starts.

While it is fair to assume it may take some time for him to return to form after he tore his Achilles last season, he will also turn 30 years old before the 2027 season and is not signed for the foreseeable future.

Indianapolis is largely playing out the string on what is turning into a lost season, and it could get more draft capital in return in an effort to accelerate the rebuilding process it is staring at if it does decide to move on from Jones.

The Ravens make logical sense, as they are a presumed contender in the AFC with Derrick Henry, Zay Jones and a talented defense. However, Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (turf toe) are both sidelined. They were forced to turn to emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano during Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Baltimore is desperate for a quarterback at this point in an effort to turn things around before it is too late in the season, and the Colts could get quite the return for Jones.

As for the Vikings, they are 6-1 in large part in spite of Kyler Murray. He is 26th in the league in QBR, per Pro Football Reference , and is lowering the ceiling for a roster that could otherwise be a legitimate Super Bowl contender.

While Jones may not be a massive upgrade, he was a backup for the team in 2024 and has some familiarity in place.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson 'Has the Power of an NBA Player' in Contract Talks, NFL Insiders Discuss Ravens Future
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson wants to remain with the Baltimore Ravens despite the lack of a contract extension agreement prior to the 2026 season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson wants to remain with the Baltimore Ravens despite the lack of a contract extension agreement prior to the 2026 season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Rapoport reported Tuesday that he "very strongly" believes Jackson wants to stay a member of the Ravens even though "other reasons" prevented an extension from being reached during the offseason (1:15 mark).

Still, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that there's plenty of uncertainty surrounding a new deal between Jackson and the Ravens.

"Lamar Jackson right now is slated to have a salary cap number in 2027 of $83.4 million. It's untenable," Schefter reported Tuesday on the Adam Schefter Podcast (17:25 mark). "Can't carry that number. Can't carry that number and construct the roster the way you want, so that has to be addressed. Lamar Jackson also has a no-trade clause. Lamar Jackson also has a no-tag clause. So, Lamar Jackson has the power of an NBA player in the NFL and he's gonna be able to dictate what he wants."

"My sense has been that he's wanted to be there, but a deal has not gotten done," he added. "A deal hasn't gotten close to being done. So there are questions from the Lamar Jackson standpoint."

Jackson currently has an $84.3 million cap hit in 2027 before he's slated to hit free agency in 2028, although the Ravens can lower that number by finalizing an extension with him.

Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer previously reported that Baltimore wanted to negotiate an extension with Jackson early in the 2026 offseason, but the star quarterback "balked" at contract discussions.

Jackson's outlook for the rest of his 2026 campaign is murky after suffering a thumb injury during the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

The two-time MVP has been one of the NFL's best quarterbacks when healthy, but he's now missed multiple games in four separate seasons since 2021.

Jackson started this year on a high note prior to the injury, completing 70.1 percent of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns compared to one interception. He also rushed for 144 yards and one score.

articles.title: Marshawn Lynch's agent doubted his $10,000 Beast Mode gamble, years later the NFL star turned a simple hoodie idea into a seven-figure business empire
articles.summary: Marshawn Lynch was known for breaking tackles and running through defenders, but he was also thinking about life beyond football.
articles.body: Marshawn Lynch was known for breaking tackles and running through defenders, but he was also thinking about life beyond football. While playing in the NFL, he took a nickname that fans already connected with him and turned it into a clothing business. His agent initially questioned whether spending $10,000 to protect the name was a wise move. Years later, Beast Mode had become a seven-figure brand, with its own stores and major retail partnerships.How did Marshawn Lynch build the Beast Mode brand while playing in the NFL?The idea behind Beast Mode came from the way people spoke about Lynch on the football field. His powerful runs and fearless style made the nickname a natural fit, and he soon realised that it could mean something beyond his performances for the Seattle Seahawks. Rather than allowing other companies to use the name and sell products without his permission, he decided to protect it.Lynch filed to trademark Beast Mode in December 2008, during his early years in the NFL. His agent, Doug Hendrickson, was not immediately convinced. At the time, Lynch was a young player, and spending around $10,000 to protect a phrase seemed like a risk when there was no guarantee that it would become a successful business.Hendrickson later shared his reaction during a 2016 interview with Sports Business Journal. He recalled Lynch telling him that he wanted to trademark the name, before explaining his own doubts: “I’m thinking to myself, ‘Alright, so it’s going to cost us 10,000 bucks. Do you really want to do this? Is it really real? And are we just throwing money away?’”Lynch, however, stuck with the idea. The trademark gave him a way to protect the name as he began building a brand around it. By 2013, before the clothing line had officially launched, he was already earning money through licensing. ESPN reported in January 2014 that Lynch had made mid-six figures from licensing Beast Mode in 2013, according to Hendrickson.The arrangement also gave Lynch control over how the name appeared on products. Sports Business Journal reported in January 2014 that companies working with him typically paid a royalty of around 20% of sales, and Lynch had to approve every design. This meant he was not simply lending his name to any product that came along.Still, he did not begin with a huge collection or an expensive retail operation. Lynch explained the simple starting point himself, saying, “I just decided to make some hoodies.” The idea was to create clothes that reflected his personality and the image people already knew from his football career.He worked with Chris Bevans, a former Nike apparel designer, who helped develop the clothing line and manage its creative direction. By January 2015, Beast Mode had around 25 products. More than 1,000 hats had also sold out through its online store and a temporary shop in Scottsdale, Arizona. The business was still young, but it was beginning to attract customers beyond people who simply wanted to support Lynch on game day.How much did Marshawn Lynch’s Beast Mode business grow, and how did it reach seven figures?Beast Mode officially launched as an apparel business during the 2014-15 NFL season. Lynch continued playing while the company worked on its products, online sales and retail plans. That meant he was building a second career at the same time as managing the demands of professional football. He also remained involved in the brand’s direction, rather than treating it as a name that could be handed over to someone else.The first major sign of its growth came in 2015, around the time Lynch and the Seahawks were preparing for Super Bowl XLIX. The brand had an online store and a temporary pop-up shop, while its clothing was gaining attention among fans. The business was also exploring licensing and retail opportunities. Chris Bevans told ESPN that, if the team built the company properly, it could reach $50 million in sales within five years. That was a future target, not a figure the company had already achieved.By June 2016, the business had reached a major milestone. Sports Business Journal, reporting on Lynch’s appearance on Showtime’s 60 Minutes Sports, described the hoodie business as a seven-figure venture. In other words, it had reached at least $1 million in business. Lynch had managed to turn a small clothing idea into a serious commercial operation while still being closely connected to the NFL.He also took the brand into physical retail. On February 5, 2016, Lynch opened his first Beast Mode store in Oakland, California, the city where he grew up. The shop sold clothing, hats, sneakers and other products connected to the brand. Oakland Mayor Libby Schaaf declared the date Beast Mode Day, giving the opening special meaning in Lynch’s hometown. The store also showed that the company was no longer relying only on online orders.One of the clearest examples of how Lynch’s football career could affect the business came in December 2019. After stepping away from the NFL, he returned to the Seattle Seahawks late in the season. The news quickly created fresh demand for Beast Mode clothing, especially products linked to his comeback.According to ESPN’s report, the website recorded around $150,000 in sales from the time Lynch’s return became official on December 23 until midday on December 27. The company’s head of operations and finance, Mitch Grossbach, said sales had reached around $20,000 in the first hour after the news was announced. He also expected December sales to be five to seven times higher than the website’s average monthly sales in the months before Lynch returned.The figures showed how closely the brand was linked to Lynch’s public image. His return to the field gave customers a new reason to buy its clothing, and the company was ready with products carrying messages such as “Back in Action” and “Unfinished Business.” The $150,000 figure was sales revenue, not confirmed profit, but it showed the scale of the sudden demand.Beast Mode took another step forward in July 2020, when Lynch announced a multi-year partnership with Fanatics. Under the deal, Fanatics would operate a new online and mobile shopping experience for the apparel company. Fanatics said it was the first time it had powered a branded e-commerce business for an athlete, celebrity or influencer.Lynch’s business journey was not a story of a clothing company that failed and suddenly became successful. It was a story of an idea that initially faced doubt, grew through careful trademark protection and began with a small range of hoodies. He built it while playing in the NFL, used the attention around his career to reach customers and later worked with a major retail partner to expand its reach.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mike Tomlin 'Not Coming Back' to NFL Coaching After Joining Media, Steelers Player Says
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin may remain in his current media role instead of eventually coming back to patrol the sidelines.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin may remain in his current media role instead of eventually coming back to patrol the sidelines.

"Guys, he's not coming back," Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward said during a Tuesday appearance on the Rich Eisen Show (0:17 mark). "He's way too comfortable. He's way too comfortable. He told me as soon as we walked in, 'I win every week now.' And I'm like, 'I get that, I get that.' I'm not gonna fight against that because that's a pretty sweet job he's got going on over there."

Tomlin spent 19 seasons as Pittsburgh's head coach from 2007-25, becoming the NFL's longest-tenured coach until he stepped down from his role on Jan. 13.

He eventually became a football analyst for NBC Sports.

Tomlin owned a 193-114-2 overall record with the Steelers, as they never posted a losing season during any year of his stint as head coach. Pittsburgh also captured a Super Bowl title during its 2008 campaign.

It's worth noting that the Steelers experienced a lack of playoff success near the end of his tenure, as their last postseason win occurred during their 2016 season despite making six playoff appearances since then.

Tomlin's overall tenure with Pittsburgh was still extremely successful, which has reportedly led to plenty of interest from NFL teams regarding his potential return to coaching.

He could end up staying in his current job, however.

articles.title: Greg Newsome, Giants Reportedly Agree to Contract Extension, Full Details Revealed
articles.summary: The New York Giants agreed to a three-year contract extension worth $46 million with cornerback Greg Newsome on Tuesday, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.
articles.body:
The New York Giants agreed to a three-year contract extension worth $46 million with cornerback Greg Newsome on Tuesday, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz .

Per Schultz, the contract contains $32 million guaranteed.

Newsome is in the midst of his first season on the Giants after signing a one-year deal with them as a free agent on March 10.

Now, he's under contract through his 2029 campaign.

Newsome won a positional battle in training camp for a starting cornerback job on the Giants and hasn't looked back.

In six games, he's racked up 25 tackles, six passes defended and one interception. Newsome has only allowed a 62.0 passer rating when targeted, according to Pro Football Focus .

He's been an important piece of a New York secondary that has helped the team compile the NFL's No. 3 pass defense , allowing a mere 184.9 yards per game through the air.

Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson previously praised Newsome's performance to begin the season.

"He's been a great impact," Wilson told reporters on Oct. 8. "I love him. Man, I believe so wholeheartedly in him and his ability. He has cultivated the room with his energy, with his effort, his attention to detail, his willingness to learn, his willingness to go the extra mile to bring guys in with – him and (safety) Jevón (Holland) bring the DBs in the group, watch extra film together."

Newsome was initially selected by the Cleveland Browns with a first-round pick in the 2021 NFL draft, operating as a starter for Cleveland until he was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars in the middle of the 2025 season.

He's amassed 49 passes defended, six tackles for loss and five interceptions across 77 career games.

Newsome's long-term future in New York is now secure as he looks to help the Giants build upon their 4-2-1 record this season.

articles.title: Carson Beck is 'Prepared To Go' After Cardinals Shake Up QB Depth Chart, HC Says
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck is one step closer to starting after the team reshuffled their quarterback depth chart on Monday.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck is one step closer to starting after the team reshuffled their quarterback depth chart on Monday.

Beck, who served as the team's emergency third-string option through the first eight games of the season, was elevated to the backup role as part of a move that named veteran Gardner Minshew as the team's starting quarterback.

"Obviously it's just behind the scenes," head coach Mike LaFleur said in his Monday press conference. "Nothing that you guys see, but I know [Beck's] prepared to go in there if need be. Again, just like Gardner, just like anyone that you ask that's going to be on this team, they're prepared as if they're going to be the starting quarterback, or they're prepared if they have to go in. I know that he has [a] full grasp of this game plan, [and] of this system."

The Cardinals selected Beck with the No. 65 overall pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, but he has yet to take any regular season snaps. Beck has been inactive for all eight games this season and has dealt with back spasms in recent weeks, but LaFleur's confidence in the young quarterback hasn't wavered.

"It's no secret, obviously, if something were to happen, it'd be nice to know what we have right there," LaFleur added. "I feel really good about where he is with his development, so if that were to come up, then obviously he'd be the next one in."

Minshew earned the starting role after he stepped in to replace incumbent starter Jacoby Brissett during the third quarter of Arizona's thrilling 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8.

Despite Minshew's stellar performance, Beck will inevitably get his opportunity at some point. The 24-year-old quarterback generated buzz after an exciting preseason debut against the Carolina Panthers in the Hall of Fame Game. Beck completed 15 of his 19 pass attempts for 188 yards and a touchdown, but a rib injury forced him to miss the remainder of the preseason. Halfway through his rookie season, he's one step closer to taking the Cardinals' starting position.

articles.title: With Lamar Jackson on IR, Ravens name undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano starting QB vs. Jaguars
articles.summary: This will be Joe Fagnano's first career start.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told the media Tuesday the team will start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The announcement comes as starting quarterback Lamar Jackson was added to injured reserve with a thumb injury , and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley was diagnosed with turf toe. Minter added that Huntley could also be going on IR.

Fagnano will be the second undrafted rookie to start under center for Baltimore in the Ravens' 32-year history, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley . The other was Anthony Brown, who started in Week 18 of the 2022 season.

In Baltimore's loss to the Buffalo Bills last week, Jackson lasted just one snap before he hit a defender on a pass attempt. He immediately came off the field holding his throwing hand and did not return.

Huntley took over, but then suffered a lower-body injury (later deemed turf toe) that forced Baltimore to use Fagnano, the team's emergency quarterback.

In relief, the rookie completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Fagnano also ran the ball three times for 3 yards.

The rookie ended his collegiate career at UConn after starting it at Maine in 2019. He played 24 career games for the Huskies, totaling 5,252 passing yards and 48 touchdowns. Fagnano is less mobile than Jackson or Huntley and rushed for just 223 yards and 4 touchdowns on 93 carries in college.

The injuries in the quarterback room aren't limited to Jackson and Huntley; Fagnano was also spotted at Tuesday's practice wearing a guard/brace on his right ankle. The injury must be minor enough that Minter felt confident naming the rookie starter for Thursday.

With the quarterback room depleted, Baltimore signed two quarterbacks to back up Fagnano. The Ravens signed Austin Reed to the practice squad on Monday and Kedon Slovis on Tuesday.

CBS Sports researcher Doug Clawson noted that Baltimore's current backup quarterback room — Fagnano, Reed and Slovis — has fewer career passing touchdowns (0) than starting running back Derrick Henry (4).

Fagnano is looking to become the first UConn quarterback since Dan Orlovsky in 2011 to win an NFL start, per Hensley .

Baltimore is 4-4 and has lost three consecutive games. The loss to Buffalo was Jackson's first game since Week 4. Now, with Fagnano under center, the Ravens face the 5-2 Jaguars, who are currently first in the AFC South.
