articles.title: Commanders' Payne, Kinlaw, McNichols Placed on Injured Reserve After Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders are placing running back Jeremy McNichols and defensive tackles Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne on injured reserve, the team announced on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders are placing running back Jeremy McNichols and defensive tackles Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne on injured reserve, the team announced on Tuesday.

Payne has spent his entire nine-year career in Washington, but he is expected to become an unrestricted free agent after this season. The 29-year-old defensive tackle was named as a potential trade candidate prior to his injury, but any chance of a move came to an end when he suffered a season-ending Jones fracture during practice last Friday.

Kinlaw missed Washington's victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night due to a knee injury he suffered against the San Francisco 49ers, but his stint on injured reserve comes as a bit of a surprise. Kinlaw tallied 13 tackles and one sack this season. He'll be eligible to return before the Commanders face the Tennessee Titans in Week 13.

Kinlaw and Payne have both served as vital parts of the Commanders defensive line over the past two seasons. Washington will now look to alleviate their losses by turning to defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton, who was designated to return from injured reserve last week.

McNichols missed multiple games earlier this season due to a quadriceps injury and was just getting adjusted to Washington's backfield rotation, but he will likely miss the remainder of the season after suffering a foot injury on Sunday. The 31-year-old running back is expected to miss multiple months, according to Tashan Reed of the Washington Post .

The Commanders' season hasn't gone as they hoped, and they're heading into a matchup against the Los Angeles Rams with with a 2-4-1 record.

articles.title: Will Jonathan Taylor, Brian Thomas Jr. get traded? How will Raiders decide on future with Maxx Crosby? What league sources are saying
articles.summary: Yahoo Sports spoke with GMs, salary-cap executives, personnel evaluators and more to take a pulse of the trade deadline landscape. The summary: Expect more m...
articles.body:
With just one week left until the 2026 NFL trade deadline, texts and calls are bouncing from front office to front office.

Multiple landscape-shifting trends have already materialized. The Chicago Bears' trade of two first-round draft picks for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons is the richest and perhaps highest-ceiling move. The New York Giants' fifth-round pick for now-starting quarterback J.J. McCarthy may net the best value.

Since the season's start, the Houston Texans have traded for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., the Dallas Cowboys have traded for cornerback Joey Porter Jr., the Seattle Seahawks have traded for left guard Quenton Nelson and the San Francisco 49ers have traded for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

Yahoo Sports spoke with NFL general managers, salary-cap executives, personnel evaluators and more to take a pulse of the trade deadline landscape. All were granted anonymity due to the competitive implications of the intel. The summary: Expect more moves during the next week. But also consider the average impact of most moves (we're not looking at you, Bears) more conservatively than initial hype may dictate.

"Usually if you're looking at this time of year, a real need, you're probably not filling it," a high-ranking NFC executive said by phone Tuesday. "You might be solidifying it. I call it, patching a leak. … You might not have planned for the Colts to be in a spiral and now their guard who is going to be a UFA, but he comes available.

"Relax and just see if there's any opportunities."

An executive from a second NFC team explained they're "always willing to make moves … if the price is right." But how often is it?

"Unless you're paying up for this stud, do any of these deals really make sense when prices are kind of flying all over the place?" the executive told Yahoo Sports. "That, to me, is never really where the best deals get made. … But if there's a [deal] that's available that feels too good to be true or the other way around, you get an offer you can't refuse?

"I think obviously you have to come into that with eyes wide open."

Is Jags' Brian Thomas Jr. 'going to be better for the second team'?

It's easy to draw parallels between Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Houston Texans receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. That begs the question: Will any team pay for Thomas the second-round draft pick (slightly discounted with a seventh/sixth-round swap) that the Texans paid the Arizona Cardinals for Harrison?

The Jaguars selected Thomas 23rd overall in the 2024 NFL Draft, 19 picks after the Cardinals selected Harrison the same year. Thomas' career peak thus far was higher, with 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns as a rookie to Harrison's 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns the same year. Each player's production and catch percentage have fallen since, and Houston banked on a reunion with Harrison's college quarterback, C.J. Stroud, reviving him. Will a fresh start revive Thomas?

"Sometimes we'll scout a player and we'll say, 'This guy is going to be better for the second team he plays for than the team that originally [drafts him] just because they kind of need a change of scenery, a wake-up call," one AFC personnel evaluator said. " 'Hey, it didn't work out and your career's about to end' — that kind of pressure.

"He definitely would fall in that category, in my opinion."

At 6-foot-2 7/8, per his scouting combine measurement, with a 4.33 40-yard dash, Thomas' size and speed allure talent evaluators. His catch reliability concerns them, Thomas falling from a 65.4% catch rate as a rookie to 52.7% last year and 45.5% this year. Thomas has also registered 19 drops, including 10 last year, per Pro Football Reference.

From the Kansas City Chiefs to the Pittsburgh Steelers, multiple top-of-their-division teams need a receiver. The Washington Commanders pique the interest of some around the league as a Harrison/Stroud-like fit that would reunite teammates and friends from Daniels' LSU Heisman days. Others wonder if Thomas' inconsistency would hurt Daniels' ability to operate a clean offense more than it'd help give the Commanders another target after Terry McLaurin's season-ending patellar tear. One high-ranking executive noted that a timing and precision offense like Coen's is unlikely to best serve Thomas as a target.

A third-round pick seems roughly what the league expects Thomas to cost, an executive from one NFC team comparing his value to that of George Pickens heading from the Steelers to the Dallas Cowboys in May 2025 for a third-round pick (with a sixth/fifth swap), while an executive from another NFC team thought the Jaguars would need to wait until the pressure of deadline day to command a third rather than a fourth. A high-ranking AFC executive noted that the Jaguars had previously shopped Thomas but earlier this season said they were no longer interested in moving him.

If the Jaguars stay put with Thomas, what will explain clinging to a player with 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns in seven games? Targets aren't Thomas' only value, as the Jaguars aim to create space for fellow receivers like Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers.

"If you trade him and then now … don't have speed, so now the defenses play more compact, it's just harder," a high-ranking NFC executive said. "It's less space. So with that being said, a third may not be enough. It's like, 'Hey, we're actually a good team. Why would we give this guy up for a third?'"

What would it take for Raiders to trade Maxx Crosby?

This question has loomed over the trade deadline since, and really even before, the Baltimore Ravens agreed to send the Las Vegas Raiders two first-round picks for Crosby in March. They infamously reneged after Crosby arrived in Baltimore and took a physical that underscored the degeneration in his knee.

The overwhelming belief around the league since: Crosby does not want to be traded. And when the Raiders opened their season 3-0, giving Crosby the main missing piece of his Raiders experience (wins), two high-ranking AFC executives agreed: Trading Crosby no longer made sense. That sentiment continued to capture conversations with executives while the Raiders were 3-1 and 3-2 before shifting slightly as the Raiders fell below (and then climbed back to) .500. So where do things stand with Crosby, who's recorded three sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and 18 quarterback hits in eight games?

"They've already traded him once," a high-ranking NFC executive said, "so I'm sure that they would listen."

Sources around the league believe that for an offer like the two first-round picks Baltimore presented, or value equivalent to a first- and second-round pick, the Raiders would pick up the phone. But the sense is not that the Raiders are actively trying to offload Crosby, who provides them value now as well as whenever they transition from Kirk Cousins to rookie first overall pick Fernando Mendoza. Executives painted a picture of what they think the Raiders may be considering: On one hand, assistant general manager Brian Stark came from the Denver Broncos, fresh off seeing how Denver's strong defense helped Bo Nix develop as a rookie. Could that sway his belief on what Mendoza needs? On the other hand, first-year head coach Klint Kubiak is the team's offensive play-caller. The more capital to collect elite linemen and skill players to run his zone scheme, the more he'll be able to execute his offensive vision.

"He's probably more valuable to keep, but if you can get two ones for him, you should flip him," an NFC executive said. "I'd probably just hang on to him because you've shown that you're already better than you thought you were… [and] then let's say Mendoza comes on at the end of the year and looks good?

"You're better off having him in 2027 and 2028 because there's a chance you can make a push at that point."

Jonathan Taylor is the most valuable skill position player in the deadline mix. That doesn't guarantee he'll be traded.

League sources stress that equating the Indianapolis Colts' trade of Nelson and Buckner with a trade of Taylor is disingenuous: Nelson and Buckner were each on expiring contracts, likely to leave this spring in free agency. Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million extension with $39 million guaranteed nearly three months ago. He's 27 years old to Nelson and Buckner's 30 and 32, respectively. And he could be a building block for a new regime that already fired general manager Chris Ballard and seems to view head coach Shane Steichen's long-term future with serious questions.

So what would it take to acquire Taylor?

Executives from multiple teams believe Taylor should command something similar to what the 49ers paid for Christian McCaffrey. On Oct. 20, 2022, the 49ers sent the Carolina Panthers 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks as well as a 2024 fifth-round pick in exchange for McCaffrey, who has since earned All-Pro honors in both of his healthy seasons.

Two caveats suggest the price could be a little lighter for Taylor than McCaffrey. First, McCaffrey's heavier usage in the passing game offsets concerns about the depreciating value of aging running backs in ways that Taylor's style might not. Secondly, the Niners were bidding against their division-rival Los Angeles Rams for McCaffrey in 2022: That auction drove the price up. Will anyone pay the Colts what it takes? Some league sources point to the Minnesota Vikings as a team that makes sense. Their defense ranks first in points allowed and second in yardage, playing like a true Super Bowl-contending unit. Their offense, meanwhile, is struggling at 27th in points scored and 29th in yards gained. The Seattle Seahawks have raised eyebrows too, though the Seahawks just showed a disinterest in paying big for Kenneth Walker III this spring. Notably, first-year Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley was part of the Seattle group that let Walker walk.

"He's a rare exception of somebody like a running back who makes such a difference that you just ... whatever they want, you just pay it because they have potential to make a run this year if they get a guy like him," an NFC executive said of the Vikings. "If they don't, they're going to stall out. They know that because they know their passing game isn't good enough right now. …

"While you got the bull by the horns, you should try to be aggressive to go, at least make sure you get to the divisional round in the playoffs."

An AFC executive underscored why the Colts should trade Taylor as well as receiver Josh Downs, rather than taking picks for only Buckner and Nelson.

"Teams that do the best job on these trades is really understanding what phase you're in and stacking," the executive said. "All of those picks combined make an intriguing rebuild. One extra third-round pick doesn't really help you."

Are Saquon Barkley, Tony Pollard viable options?

No one's suggesting that the current iteration of Eagles running back Saquon Barkley nor Titans running back Tony Pollard can elevate a team like Taylor can. Each would be cheaper than Taylor accordingly, but Barkley no longer makes sense for a trade. League sources weren't surprised to hear Barkley say on Sunday night that he's been told he won't be traded. While overwhelming league sentiment is that the Eagles should aim to recoup value, and especially salary cap space from their roster, amid their injury-riddled lost season, Barkley's hamstring and back injuries tank his value likely beyond the point of a helpful return. Before his injuries worsened, executives pegged Barkley's value with his contract as ranging from a second to a fourth-round pick.

Hurting the Eagles' case is that while some positions last well from season to season, the league's view on running-back depreciation tends to limit running-back trades to teams wanting to maximize their acquisition this year. Barkley's limitations hamper that hope.

"That is one position the draft always looks better because age is such a negative thing," an AFC talent evaluator said. "And I'd say running back or skill positions like receiver, usually the need is immediate so they don't compare. If someone acquired Saquon or [Taylor], I think it'll be for this season more than anything."

The Eagles still could shop players. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo, tight end Dallas Goedert and offensive lineman Tyler Steen are all in the last year of their contracts. Ojomo drew high-value interest before the season, per a league source, but the Eagles declined. With their 2026 season spiraling, would they reconsider sending Ojomo away for something like a second-round pick?

"I think they would probably take the second now," a high-ranking executive from another NFC team said. "But probably going into the year, they'd be like, OK, if we're winning, you're at least planning on trying to win. And then you're like, 'Well, we're not.'"

To round out the running back conversation, Pollard is a cost-effective, healthy and still potentially valuable back who could give a team solid depth. His 595 yards and six touchdowns rushing this season each rank ninth in the league, and Tennessee could seek value for a player likely to walk this spring anyway. A team renting Pollard for the second half of the season might need to pay a fourth or slightly more to award the Titans more than the compensatory pick they'd otherwise get.

Odds and ends: Chargers questions, why Jeffery Simmons isn't your average DL trade, more

League wisdom says the last winless team, the Los Angeles Chargers, should trade players before the deadline to amass the capital needed to rebound from their 0-7 start. But who would this franchise trade? Edge rusher Tuli Tuipulotu is in the final year of his rookie deal, following up his 2025 13-sack season with an interception, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery in seven games so far. He also leads all edge rushers in run-stop win rate, per ESPN's metric. Executives from multiple teams think he'd draw value akin to a second-round draft pick even with just half a year left on his deal. But trading away young edge rushers is a risky proposition, and the Chargers are "a relatively conservative bunch," as one high-ranking NFC executive said. Executives and evaluators believe it would make little sense, however, for the Chargers not to offload 35-year-old Khalil Mack . He's also up after this season and regardless of the pick back, trading the remainder of Mack's $18 million salary is worth it, they say. Mack could help a team needing pass rush, but at this stage of his career, "I wouldn't count on him as a game-changer," the high-ranking NFC executive said.

Falcons safety Jessie Bates III could be a win-win option for a contending team. The Falcons drafted safety Xavier Watts in the third round last year and safety Billy Bowman in the fourth last year before trading for Sydney Brown this spring. Atlanta's depth at the position, paired with their 3-5 record and quarterback questions, should help the Falcons rationalize trading away an impact defender. In eight games, Bates has 46 tackles, three forced fumbles, one fumble recovery touchdown and one interception. He could immediately elevate a contender that's currently stronger on offense than defense. One NFC executive pointed to the Buffalo Bills as a fit to narrow the gap between their powerhouse offense and shaky defense, while an executive from another NFC team thought the Bills would be more interested in pass-rushing help. (The Bills released safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson on Tuesday , opening another potential case for Bates.) Executives pegged the likely price to rent Bates at a third-round pick, with the possibility to creep to a second.

Executives across the league remain split on whether they'd have traded two first-round picks for Jeffery Simmons , who starred in his Monday night debut with the Chicago Bears. Simmons' six tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss and pass deflection wreaked havoc on the Seahawks in a 34-17 decision. Some executives believe the price was too steep, pegging Simmons' value as closer to a first- and second-round pick or "one and change." The Bears became the first team in the modern draft era to spend two first-round picks on an interior defensive lineman. But one high-ranking NFC executive said they respect the Bears recognizing their window and chasing it. A talent evaluator from another NFC team explained why they're more comfortable trading for a 29-year-old defensive tackle than a speed rusher. "As a speed rusher, there is going to be a level of depreciation that you're going to expect from this player regardless … " the evaluator said. "These large prototype, explosive, powerful defensive linemen I would say do tend to have a level of normal regression that I think can protect your investment."

articles.title: ‘I Think He Would Accept a Trade to Miami’ — Analyst Boldly Predicts Dolphins Will Acquire Lamar Jackson in Blockbuster Deal
articles.summary: Nick Wright has already penciled Lamar Jackson into a different Week 1 lineup for 2027. The FOX Sports analyst believes the Dolphins could make the biggest m...
articles.body:
Nick Wright has already penciled Lamar Jackson into a different Week 1 lineup for 2027. The FOX Sports analyst believes the Dolphins could make the biggest move of the next offseason by acquiring Baltimore's two-time MVP.

With Jackson facing another extended absence and his contract approaching a decision point, Wright sees Miami as a destination that could appeal to both the quarterback and a franchise searching for answers.

Nick Wright Predicts Lamar Jackson Will Become Dolphins' Starter

Appearing on "The Herd," Wright made a direct prediction about where Jackson will play next season.

"I think Lamar Jackson is the Week 1 starting quarterback next year for the Miami Dolphins," Wright said in the clip shared by the show .

He built his case around Miami potentially holding a valuable draft pick, its financial direction and Jackson's connection to Florida.

"I think the Dolphins are going to have a top-three pick. The Dolphins cleaned up their cap," Wright said.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

"I think he would accept a trade to Miami because of the Florida roots. I think that might be where this is headed."

Miami fell to 1-6 after Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England. That record makes a high selection plausible, although the final draft order remains months away.

Wright's proposal would give the Dolphins an established quarterback with a résumé few potential acquisitions could match. It would also require Baltimore to entertain moving the player around whom it has built its offense.

That distinction matters. Wright was predicting a possible outcome, and the supplied clip contained no announcement of trade discussions or a request from Jackson.

Jackson's deal includes a no-trade clause, giving his willingness to approve a destination practical significance. His contract runs through 2027, so a move next offseason would require a transaction while he remains under contract.

Jackson's Latest Injury Raises Difficult Questions for Baltimore

The discussion followed Jackson's thumb injury on Baltimore's opening offensive snap against Buffalo. He had just returned after missing three games with an ankle injury.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Jackson would require surgery and go on injured reserve, leaving open the possibility that his season could be over.

Baltimore lost 36-10 and dropped to 4-4. Tyler Huntley also exited with a toe injury, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut.

Those circumstances have sharpened questions about Jackson's long-term future in Baltimore , with the organization facing decisions about both its immediate quarterback needs and its next contract commitment.

"Nobody's blaming Lamar for the injuries, but what do you do with Lamar? Would you extend him?" Wright asked.

"I mean, this is one of the trickiest situations we've ever had in the NFL."

Wright emphasized the quality of Jackson's healthy seasons, citing his first-team All-Pro selections and two league MVP awards. His concern centered on how often Baltimore can count on having that player available.

"When he's out there, he's as dynamic a regular-season player as we've ever seen, but he's not out there that often," he said.

For Miami, acquiring Jackson would mean weighing that same concern against the opportunity to add an exceptional talent. For Baltimore, any proposal would have to justify surrendering a quarterback capable of defining the franchise.

Wright has picked his destination. The Dolphins' remaining season will help determine whether they possess the draft capital to make that prediction worth a serious phone call.

articles.title: George Pickens trade update from NFL insider raises eyebrows after Cowboys loss
articles.summary: George Pickens trade news: The latest on the talk surrounding a possible trade from the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys fell in yet another close game on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals , 33-30 in an overtime loss. That puts Dallas at a 3-5 record for the season, which obviously isn't a good look.

Heading into their next game against the 2-6 Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, there are a lot of questions about what owner and general manager Jerry Jones may do before the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline. One of the big players that he could possibly move is wide receiver George Pickens. So, will it happen?

NFL insider shares latest update on George Pickens trade rumors

With all the talk about Pickens possibly getting traded before the trade deadline, one NFL insider is sharing what he's heard. Appearing on the Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said , "I was told the Dallas Cowboys aren't trading George Pickens."

Zachary Krueger of NBC Sports adds that Rapoport also said, "As of right now, there's nothing there," as far as a potential trade involving the player.

"Pickens, who is playing out the season on the franchise tag, hasn't produced at the level he did in 2025 when he broke out for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, but he remains a focal point in the offense despite his underwhelming production," Krueger adds. "Pickens still ranks 14th in the league among all receivers in targets and is 12th in total air yards. Despite the Cowboys' disappointing 3-5 record, they remain in the race to win what has been an underwhelming NFC East."

He adds, "With team owner Jerry Jones saying earlier that Pickens needs to be targeted more, it's safe to assume he will remain with the Cowboys for the season."

So, all of that talk and buzz about Pickens getting moved may amount to nothing. But never say never until Nov. 10 has come and gone.

articles.title: There’s 1 NFL Hall of Fame QB who should replace Troy Aikman on MNF
articles.summary: This is the most logical choice to replace Aikman on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
The future of Troy Aikman on ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast has become one of the biggest sports media stories of the NFL season. With Aikman's contract set to expire after Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027, speculation about his replacement is heating up. While several names have been mentioned, there is one candidate who makes more sense than anyone else: Peyton Manning.

Peyton Manning is the obvious choice to replace Troy Aikman

There has been plenty of discussion about who ESPN could bring in to replace Aikman if he leaves the network. Greg Olsen has emerged as a popular candidate, while Jason Kelce could also be an option given his existing role on the Monday Night Countdown panel.

Tony Romo is another name that could generate plenty of attention. The former Cowboys quarterback recently became available after parting ways with CBS. Replacing one Dallas quarterback with another would certainly be an interesting storyline, but Romo is not the answer.

Instead, ESPN should make a serious push to bring Manning into the traditional Monday Night Football booth.

The Hall of Fame quarterback already has an established relationship with ESPN through the ManningCast, which he hosts alongside his brother, Eli Manning. The alternate broadcast has become a familiar part of ESPN's Monday Night Football coverage, giving Peyton plenty of experience discussing NFL games in front of a national audience.

Manning also brings the credibility, personality, football knowledge, and name recognition that ESPN should want in its lead NFL broadcast booth. Pairing him with Joe Buck would give the network an opportunity to create another high-profile broadcasting partnership.

ESPN should make Peyton Manning its top priority

There is no shortage of potential candidates, but Manning should be at the top of ESPN's list.

Greg Olsen is a legitimate option, and his past experience as Fox's lead analyst (before Tom Brady) makes him an attractive candidate. However, Olsen doesn't bring the same combination of Hall of Fame playing experience, national recognition, and existing ESPN relationship as Manning.

The biggest obstacle could be convincing Manning to take on the traditional broadcast role. He has previously declined opportunities to join a regular NFL broadcast booth, and his current arrangement with ESPN allows him to work alongside Eli without the demands of traveling to every game. ESPN would have to make an offer compelling enough to change that.

Still, if Aikman is officially finished with Monday Night Football after the Super Bowl, there should be one name at the top of the replacement conversation.

Peyton Manning is the logical choice. ESPN should make him its priority, and there really isn't a close second.

articles.title: Ravens have 3 encouraging trends to build on against the Jaguars
articles.summary: Justice Hill's versatility, defensive takeaways and Rasheen Ali's return ability give the Ravens positive trends to carry into Week 9
articles.body:
The most encouraging thing about the Baltimore Ravens ' 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills might be that the final score doesn't tell the entire story . Baltimore had stretches when it competed with one of the NFL's better teams, and several individual performances offered something worth carrying into Thursday night's matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars .

There is no disguising how much went wrong in Buffalo , particularly after Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley left with injuries. The offense never found its footing, and the defense eventually spent too much time on the field. Still, the Ravens cannot afford to treat the entire afternoon as a failure.

With a short week and with Joe Fagnano making his first start at quarterback , they need to identify what worked and find ways to build on it. The challenge now is turning isolated positive moments into repeatable production. Baltimore needs more than a few standout plays if it hopes to change its season's direction.

Justice Hill was one of the few bright spots in another Ravens loss that was honestly tough to watch. He averaged five yards per carry, gaining 15 yards on three attempts, and added four receptions for 20 yards. His contributions weren't enough to change the outcome, but they showed Baltimore has another way to generate offense when its primary options aren't producing.

Derrick Henry hasn't consistently looked like the dominant force Baltimore expected, and the receiving corps has struggled to find reliable production beyond Zay Flowers. Even Flowers was held without a catch against Buffalo. Hill adds a different dimension because he can contribute as both a runner and receiver, creating opportunities for a quarterback with limited experience.

The Ravens shouldn't treat Hill as a replacement for Henry or suddenly make him the offense's centerpiece. However, getting him more involved would give Jacksonville another player to account for and help Baltimore avoid becoming too predictable. His versatility could be particularly valuable with a rookie quarterback starting.

The defense must continue its ball-hawking approach

Baltimore finally generated multiple takeaways against Buffalo, something the defense desperately needed after going through a stretch without consistently creating turnovers. Broderick Washington Jr. intercepted Josh Allen, setting up Henry's first-quarter touchdown, while Roquan Smith forced a fumble that T.J. Tampa recovered. Those plays gave the Ravens opportunities to stay in a game that eventually got away from them.

The significance goes beyond the individual statistics. Washington's interception came on a tipped pass, while Tampa was in position to recover the football after Smith forced the fumble. Both plays required defenders to recognize an opportunity and finish it. Baltimore needs more of that awareness and urgency against Jacksonville, especially with Lawrence playing confidently under Coen.

The Ravens cannot rely on turnovers to compensate for every offensive shortcoming, but creating extra possessions would take pressure off an offense that's operating with an inexperienced quarterback. Jacksonville has shown it can score in bunches, so Baltimore needs its defense to disrupt that rhythm rather than simply trying to survive each possession.

Rasheen Ali's explosiveness can change field position

Rasheen Ali gave Baltimore a much-needed spark with a 59-yard kickoff return, the team's longest of the season. He finished with 147 kickoff return yards on five attempts, providing an important source of production on a day when the offense managed just 144 total yards. His return helped put the offense in a better starting position for Joe Fagnano's first possession.

That contribution deserves more attention than it usually gets. When an offense is struggling to sustain drives, a productive return unit can shorten the field and create scoring opportunities without requiring the quarterback to engineer a long possession. Ali has shown he can provide that kind of spark, and Baltimore should keep giving him opportunities to make plays.

The Ravens will need every advantage they can find against Jacksonville. Ali's ability to flip field position could become especially important if Baltimore struggles to move the ball consistently. The return game has offered a positive development, and the team needs to preserve that production while cleaning up the mistakes elsewhere on special teams.

Baltimore needs to turn small positives into consistent production

The Ravens won't erase their problems in one game, especially with the injuries and uncertainty at quarterback. However, a few encouraging developments are worth carrying into Jacksonville.

Hill can provide versatility, the defense has shown it can create takeaways, and Ali has given the return game a needed boost. Those contributions need to become part of a more complete performance. Baltimore cannot afford to have its positive moments disappear for long stretches, especially against a Jacksonville team coming off a convincing victory. The Ravens need to build on what worked in Buffalo and give themselves a chance to compete for four quarters.

With undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano making his first NFL start Thursday night, the Ravens cannot afford to consistently put their offense in difficult situations against a Jacksonville Jaguars team coming off a 42-7 victory over the Indianapolis Colts. Baltimore must find ways to shorten the field, create manageable down-and-distance situations, and generate additional possessions to take pressure off its inexperienced quarterback. Justice Hill's versatility could provide Fagnano with reliable short-yardage options, while Rasheen Ali's explosiveness in the return game could give the offense favorable starting field position. The defense also must build on its two takeaways against Buffalo, creating opportunities for Derrick Henry and the running game to control possession. Against a Jacksonville offense that can score quickly, the Ravens need contributions from all three phases rather than asking Fagnano to consistently engineer lengthy scoring drives.

articles.title: New Cowboys Trade Rumors Reveal Plans for George Pickens Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are 3-5 and look nothing like a legitimate contender. George Pickens is playing on the franchise tag and may go elsewhere during the upcoming offseason.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are 3-5 and look nothing like a legitimate contender. George Pickens is playing on the franchise tag and may go elsewhere during the upcoming offseason.

Logic dictates there could be a trade in the making before the NFL's Nov. 10 deadline.

"I was told there's nothing here and that it is not happening," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported during an appearance on Tuesday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show . "… As of right now, literally nothing there. … The way the Cowboys' division is, it is wide open. I would be surprised to see them trading a playmaker."

Rapoport's final point is important, as the Cowboys are still within striking distance of the first-place New York Giants.

New York is 4-2-1 but is relying on J.J. McCarthy at quarterback with Jaxson Dart sidelined by injury. It also still has to play the Cowboys on the road in Week 17, meaning Dallas will have an opportunity to pick up a critical late-season head-to-head result.

Given the amount of talent on the Cowboys' roster with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, Pickens and Javonte Williams, among others, it wouldn't be particularly surprising if they rallied from their slow start and threatened for the division crown.

Yet trading Pickens would be quite the blow for those chances.

The 2025 Pro Bowler has 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns through eight games this season after finishing with career-highs across the board last year with 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns.

There is obvious chemistry in place with Prescott, and trading him ahead of the deadline would prevent the Cowboys from perhaps engaging in long-term contract discussions with the star receiver down the line.

What's more, team owner Jerry Jones told 105.3 The Fan he doesn't see the team making any notable trades in the immediate future:

Between Jones' comments and Rapoport's reporting, it would certainly be stunning if Pickens finished the season anywhere but Dallas.

articles.title: 49ers trade targets: 4 players San Francisco could pursue at NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: Will the 49ers be buyers at the 2026 NFL trade deadline? If they are, they will likely try to upgrade these positions.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have an opportunity to improve their roster ahead of the league's trade deadline on Nov. 10 .

The Niners return from the bye week ready to bring their former defensive lineman DeForest Buckner back into the fold after completing a trade with the Indianapolis Colts , bringing the 32-year-old back to the Bay Area.

The deal for Buckner was just a start; San Francisco isn't expected to be done yet. The 49ers' main concern is depth and making sure they have enough bodies to make it through the regular season and into the postseason.

The 49ers are 6-1 but have dealt with a ton of injuries throughout the year, mainly at defensive line and wide receiver. Those are areas where San Francisco could use more depth.

The Niners tried to bring back former receiver Jauan Jennings in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings, but Jennings denied the trade.

Receivers that have been out for the 49ers include Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, DeMarcus Robinson and tight end Jake Tonges. Deebo Samuel Sr. is expected to be ready to go after sitting with a right hamstring injury. KhaDarel Hodge was signed to the 49ers' practice squad and the 32-year-old wide receiver might have a chance to play against the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 9.

49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk hired a new agent , bringing Drew Rosenhaus on his team in an attempt to return to the NFL. Still, San Francisco is likely not an option.

Although things aren't terrible on the defensive side of the ball, San Francisco could use upgrades defensively, at least more help in their pass rush and on the edge.

The 49ers defense is 20th in sacks and 27th in takeaways, including 29th in interceptions and 19th in forced fumbles. San Francisco's run defense allows 89 yards per game, the 5th-fewest in the league. They're third in total rush yards with 623 through 7 games. They've allowed the fewest rushing touchdowns, three.

Still, the injuries the 49ers have experienced still affect them. They've been dealt injuries to Nick Bosa, Alfred Collins, C.J. West, Sam Okuayinonu, Mikail Kamara and Andrew Farmer II. All have missed time going in and out of the lineup. The 49ers only recently got Mykel Williams back from an ACL injury.

Still, the 49ers may consider a move ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline. Who could they target if they keep buying? Here's a look at the top trade options San Francisco could pursue.

NFL TRADE DEADLINE LIVE UPDATES: Latest news and rumors on Tuesday

Cheerleaders, celebrities, fans and mascots at NFL games during 2026 season

Brian Thomas Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars, WR

The 49ers need a WR and Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. could use a fresh start after a slow start to the season. In his third season, Thomas, through seven games, has recorded 10 receptions, 117 yards and two touchdowns. He averages 11.7 yards per catch.

He earned a Pro Bowl selection during his rookie year in 2024 for season stats of 87 catches, 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns in 17 games. Then he had a sophomore slump. He played 14 games and only tallied 48 catches, 707 yards and two touchdowns.

San Francisco needs more young weapons in their aging WR room after all the injuries. Thomas would be a dream to team up with Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and tight end George Kittle.

Khalil Mack is 35 and was the 5th overall pick selected by the then-Oakland Raiders in the 2014 NFL Draft. The former NFL Defensive Player of the Year is older but can still provide a spark as a vet. Mack built his career as a pass rusher, compiling 116 career sacks and ranking seventh all-time among active players.

Mack has done just about everything in the NFL, except win a Super Bowl. He was the 2016 Defensive Player of the Year, a nine-time Pro Bowl selection and a three-time All-Pro linebacker. He might thrive in a role where he can win a coveted Super Bowl ring.

The Los Angeles Chargers are winless. Mack seems to be nearing the end of his career but could get a boost in a winning situation. Mack could add more depth to the 49ers' defensive front. He has three sacks and 11 tackles this season. His snaps might be limited, but he could be a force rushing the passer and even spell Nick Bosa when he returns.

Will McDonald IV could be the power punch on the edge that the 49ers are looking for. He plays a complementary role in New York, but he can be effective when he sees snaps. McDonald is a 6-foot-4, 245-pound pass rusher who has 23.5 career sacks and four forced fumbles in 54 games.

That kind of addition could give San Francisco another weapon on the line as they look to fill the void left by injuries. McDonald possesses a skill set that would complement the 49ers' existing defensive line with a healthy Keion White, Gracen Halton, Osa Odighizuwa, Romello Height and Mykel Williams.

So far in 2026, he has three sacks and seven total tackles.

The 49ers already knocked on the Colts' door to make a trade; why not do it again? San Francisco needs wide receivers and Indianapolis is apparently undergoing a fire sale. The 49ers would do themselves a favor by going after Josh Downs. The 25-year-old wide receiver has 30 catches, 330 receiving yards and one touchdown this season.

He would give the Niners another fresh look at wideout lining up predominantly in the slot. He's shifty in his cuts and is another QB-friendly target. He would be a solid addition for San Francisco as they ease back Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel from injury. The 49ers could await for their rookie De'Zhaun Stribling to return but in the meantime, a trade would mean they don't have to rush him back, or put additional pressure on him to perform.

articles.title: Raiders owner announces approach toward starting Fernando Mendoza
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza with the number one overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. However, the former Heisman Trophy winner has been rel...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza with the number one overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. However, the former Heisman Trophy winner has been relegated to backup duties while veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins runs the offense.

Cousins has had an impressive season individually, throwing 19 passing touchdowns and posting a 101.4 quarterback rating, but the Raiders are just 4-4 on the season and on the outside looking in at the current AFC playoff picture. Many are wondering when Vegas will make the switch to get Mendoza game experience, but fans shouldn't look to team owner Mark Davis to pressure the coaching staff into making a change.

"From me, there's absolutely no pressure whatsoever," Davis told CNBC Sport's Michael Ozanian on Monday.

"Today, there's a lot of pressure put on teams when they draft a guy No. 1 that you have to play him right away," Davis added. "That's why I think we were so fortunate to get Kirk Cousins as someone who could bridge the gap and let this young man learn a lot about what football is in the pros, the speed of the game, and the things that have to be done."

Although Davis is taking a patient approach with the quarterback, it's not because he isn't picking things up.

"He's picking it up great, but I think we're fortunate that he doesn't have to go out and play," Davis said. "I've seen quarterbacks get fast-tracked onto the field, and they may do well, but they don't learn all the intricacies of footwork and everything else that it takes. So they're limited in their development, maybe throughout their career."

Whenever Mendoza does get the nod, Davis thinks he has the intangibles and leadership traits to flourish in the NFL.

"I tell people jokingly, if he can play football, he's going to be amazing," Davis said. "Because he's got every other intangible that you would want in a person. He's a hard worker. He's a sponge."
